paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of a High-Strength Ti-4Al-2Fe-3Cu Alloy Fabricated by Sintering and Hot Extrusion

The blended powder having a nominal composition of Ti-4Al-2Fe-3Cu was die-pressed into a cylindrical powder compact with a diameter of 26 mm, a height of 25 mm, and a relative density of 87 pct.

The powder compact was sintered at 1200 /C176C for 1 hour in a vacuum furnace to achieve a relative density of 96 pct. The nominal heating and cooling rates were both programmed at 10 /C176C/min, but the cooling rate was lower at temperatures below 500 /C176C due to the limitation of furnace cooling.
A bulk Ti-4Al-2Fe-3Cu alloy was fabricated by combination of vacuum sintering of a blend TiH2, Al, Fe, and Cu powders and hot extrusion of the sintered powder compact.

The sintered powder compact was induction heated to 1200 /C176C, held at the temperature for 5 minutes, and then extruded into a circular rod with an extrusion ratio of 9:1. The heating, holding, and extrusion of the sintered powder compact were all performed within a glovebox filled with argon.
